official_scope: properties and processes of Earth's fresh waters
design_notes: Concept densities range from 9 to 13 per topic, reflecting real differences in the breadth of tested skills. Topics 4, 5, and 8 are denser because they carry quantitative streamflow, groundwater, and applied monitoring demands. Topic 7 is intentionally narrower at 9 concepts because paleohydrologic evidence types are more consolidated. No topic is a stub; no concepts are duplicated across topics.

topics.title: Hydrologic cycle, water budgets, and climatic controls

concepts.title: Freshwater reservoirs and global distribution
concepts.description: Distinguish the major freshwater reservoirs by volume and percent of total freshwater, including glaciers, groundwater, lakes, soil moisture, atmosphere, and rivers.

concepts.title: Hydrologic flux definitions
concepts.description: Define precipitation, evaporation, transpiration, evapotranspiration, infiltration, percolation, runoff, and baseflow as distinct water-cycle fluxes.

concepts.title: Residence time calculation
concepts.description: Calculate mean residence time by dividing reservoir volume by the average flux rate and interpret turnover times for different freshwater stores.

concepts.title: Basin water budget equation
concepts.description: Apply the water balance equation P = R + ET + ΔS to a drainage basin and solve for an unknown term using given data.

concepts.title: Precipitation mechanisms
concepts.description: Distinguish orographic, frontal, cyclonic, and convectional precipitation and predict where each occurs relative to topography and air masses.

concepts.title: Potential vs actual evapotranspiration
concepts.description: Distinguish potential evapotranspiration from actual evapotranspiration and identify water-limited versus energy-limited conditions from climate data.

concepts.title: Infiltration controls and capacity
concepts.description: Explain how soil texture, antecedent moisture, slope, and vegetation control infiltration capacity and generate Hortonian overland flow.

concepts.title: Soil water storage and plant availability
concepts.description: Relate field capacity, wilting point, and available water capacity to soil texture and interpret water availability for plants.

concepts.title: Runoff generation pathways
concepts.description: Distinguish overland flow, throughflow, and groundwater flow as runoff generation pathways and identify conditions favoring each.

concepts.title: Snowpack accumulation, storage, and ablation
concepts.description: Describe seasonal snowpack accumulation, ablation, and snow water equivalent as freshwater storage that controls spring melt runoff.

concepts.title: Climatic controls on freshwater distribution
concepts.description: Relate Hadley circulation, ITCZ position, monsoons, and rain shadows to global patterns of precipitation, aridity, and freshwater availability.

concepts.title: Watershed and drainage divide identification
concepts.description: Identify watershed, drainage basin, and catchment boundaries from topographic maps using drainage divides and contour lines.

concepts.title: Drainage patterns and geologic controls
concepts.description: Identify dendritic, trellis, rectangular, radial, parallel, annular, and deranged drainage patterns from maps and infer underlying geology or structure.

concepts.title: Strahler stream ordering
concepts.description: Assign Strahler stream order at confluences using the same-order joining rule and interpret basin magnitude.

concepts.title: Shreve stream ordering
concepts.description: Assign Shreve magnitude as the sum of upstream links at each confluence and contrast Shreve magnitude with Strahler order.

concepts.title: Drainage density calculation
concepts.description: Calculate drainage density as total stream length divided by basin area and interpret climatic, lithologic, and vegetation controls.

concepts.title: Bifurcation ratio
concepts.description: Calculate bifurcation ratio from stream order counts and interpret typical values and network branching characteristics.

concepts.title: Basin relief, elongation, and ruggedness
concepts.description: Compute basin relief, relief ratio, elongation ratio, and ruggedness number and relate them to flood response and basin shape.

concepts.title: Headward erosion and stream capture
concepts.description: Recognize stream piracy, wind gaps, and elbows of capture and explain how headward erosion reorganizes drainage networks.

concepts.title: Base level and knickpoints
concepts.description: Define ultimate and local base level and predict channel profile adjustments to base-level fall or rise, including knickpoint migration.

concepts.title: Perennial, intermittent, and ephemeral streams
concepts.description: Classify streams by flow permanence and link perennial, intermittent, and ephemeral reaches to water-table position and climate.

concepts.title: Longitudinal profile and graded stream concept
concepts.description: Describe the concave-up longitudinal profile of a graded stream and identify disruptions such as knickpoints or base-level changes.

topics.title: Fluvial sediment processes, channel form, and landforms

concepts.title: Hjulström curve interpretation
concepts.description: Interpret the Hjulström curve to predict erosion, transport, and deposition for given particle sizes and stream velocities.

concepts.title: Dissolved, suspended, and bed load
concepts.description: Distinguish dissolved, suspended, and bed load by transport mechanism and identify the dominant load type from stream appearance and sediment supply.

concepts.title: Settling velocity and suspension
concepts.description: Apply Stokes settling velocity to explain why clay and silt remain suspended while sand settles rapidly in flowing water.

concepts.title: Stream competence and capacity
concepts.description: Distinguish competence, the largest particle a stream can move, from capacity, the total sediment load a stream can carry.

concepts.title: Bedforms and flow regime
concepts.description: Identify ripples, dunes, plane bed, antidunes, and pool-riffle sequences and relate them to lower versus upper flow regime.

concepts.title: At-a-station and downstream hydraulic geometry
concepts.description: Describe how width, depth, and velocity change with discharge at a station and downstream using hydraulic geometry relationships.

concepts.title: Straight, meandering, braided, and anastomosing channels
concepts.description: Explain why channels adopt straight, meandering, braided, or anastomosing patterns based on slope, sediment supply, and bank erodibility.

concepts.title: Meander geometry, migration, and cutoffs
concepts.description: Identify point bars, cut banks, pools, and riffles in meandering channels; calculate sinuosity and explain oxbow lake formation by cutoff.

concepts.title: Floodplain depositional features
concepts.description: Recognize natural levees, crevasse splays, backswamps, and yazoo tributaries from topographic maps, air photos, or descriptions.

concepts.title: Fluvial terrace classification
concepts.description: Distinguish strath and fill terraces and paired versus unpaired terraces from cross sections and map patterns.

concepts.title: Alluvial fan formation and deposits
concepts.description: Explain alluvial fan formation at mountain-front slope breaks and identify debris-flow, sheetflood, and sieve deposits.

concepts.title: Freshwater delta formation and types
concepts.description: Describe delta formation where streams enter lakes or reservoirs and distinguish river-dominated, wave-dominated, and Gilbert-type deltas.

concepts.title: Channel avulsion
concepts.description: Define avulsion and recognize how crevasse splays, floodplain slope, and aggradation can cause sudden channel relocation.

concepts.title: Discharge equation
concepts.description: Calculate stream discharge as the product of mean velocity and cross-sectional area using the continuity equation Q = A v.

concepts.title: Velocity measurement and vertical profile
concepts.description: Describe vertical velocity profiles and select one-point or two-point current-meter methods for measuring mean velocity.

concepts.title: Manning equation for mean velocity
concepts.description: Apply the Manning equation to estimate mean velocity from hydraulic radius, water-surface slope, and channel roughness.

concepts.title: Stage and rating curve interpretation
concepts.description: Interpret a stage-discharge rating curve to estimate discharge from stage and recognize limitations such as loop rating shifts.

concepts.title: Storm hydrograph components
concepts.description: Identify baseflow, rising limb, crest, recession limb, and lag time on a storm hydrograph and describe what each part represents.

concepts.title: Flood recurrence interval
concepts.description: Calculate flood recurrence interval from rank and record length using R = (n+1)/m and interpret the meaning of a 100-year flood.

concepts.title: Annual exceedance probability
concepts.description: Convert recurrence interval to annual exceedance probability and calculate the probability of at least one flood over a design period.

concepts.title: Unit hydrograph interpretation
concepts.description: Interpret unit hydrograph assumptions and use a unit hydrograph to predict runoff timing and peak for a given storm depth and duration.

concepts.title: Flash floods, river floods, and ice-jam floods
concepts.description: Distinguish flash floods, regional river floods, ice-jam floods, and dam-failure floods by cause, timing, basin size, and hazard.

concepts.title: Baseflow separation
concepts.description: Separate baseflow from direct runoff on a storm hydrograph using graphical methods and interpret the resulting baseflow contribution.

concepts.title: Stream gauging methods
concepts.description: Describe current-meter, acoustic Doppler, dilution, and slope-area methods for measuring discharge and select an appropriate method for field conditions.

concepts.title: Flow duration curve
concepts.description: Construct and interpret flow duration curves to characterize low-flow and high-flow frequency and exceedance percentiles.

concepts.title: Porosity and permeability
concepts.description: Distinguish porosity from permeability and identify primary and secondary porosity and effective porosity in aquifer materials.

concepts.title: Darcy's law
concepts.description: Calculate groundwater discharge using Darcy's law Q = K A (dh/dl) and determine hydraulic gradient from water-level data.

concepts.title: Hydraulic conductivity and transmissivity
concepts.description: Distinguish hydraulic conductivity from transmissivity and compute transmissivity as T = K b using aquifer thickness.

concepts.title: Vadose, phreatic, and capillary fringe
concepts.description: Distinguish the vadose zone, phreatic zone, water table, and capillary fringe and predict water-table position from saturation diagrams.

concepts.title: Aquifer types and confining units
concepts.description: Classify unconfined, confined, perched, and artesian aquifers and identify aquitards and aquicludes from cross sections.

concepts.title: Groundwater flow direction from water-table maps
concepts.description: Infer groundwater flow direction from water-table contours and draw flow lines perpendicular to equipotential lines.

concepts.title: Recharge and discharge areas
concepts.description: Identify recharge and discharge zones from water-table configuration and distinguish gaining from losing stream reaches.

concepts.title: Well drawdown and cone of depression
concepts.description: Describe drawdown, cone of depression, and well interference and explain specific capacity as a measure of well performance.

concepts.title: Spring classification
concepts.description: Classify springs by origin as gravity, contact, fault, artesian, karst, or depression springs and identify conditions that form each type.

concepts.title: Carbonate dissolution reactions
concepts.description: Write carbonate dissolution reactions and explain the role of carbon dioxide, pH, and limestone solubility in karst formation.

concepts.title: Karst landforms
concepts.description: Identify sinkholes, uvalas, poljes, tower karst, disappearing streams, and karst springs on maps, photos, and block diagrams.

concepts.title: Caves and speleothem formation
concepts.description: Describe cave formation in the phreatic and vadose zones and distinguish stalactites, stalagmites, columns, and flowstone by growth environment.

concepts.title: Lake thermal stratification
concepts.description: Identify epilimnion, metalimnion, thermocline, and hypolimnion from temperature profiles and describe seasonal stratification patterns.

concepts.title: Lake mixing regimes
concepts.description: Classify lakes as amictic, monomictic, dimictic, polymictic, or meromictic based on annual mixing and stratification patterns.

concepts.title: Lake basin origin types
concepts.description: Identify lake basins by origin, including glacial, tectonic, volcanic, landslide, oxbow, solution, and artificial lakes.

concepts.title: Lake trophic state classification
concepts.description: Classify lakes as oligotrophic, mesotrophic, eutrophic, or hypereutrophic using nutrient concentrations, Secchi depth, chlorophyll, and dissolved oxygen.

concepts.title: Dissolved oxygen and temperature profiles
concepts.description: Interpret dissolved oxygen and temperature profiles and explain orthograde versus clinograde oxygen curves and hypolimnetic oxygen depletion.

concepts.title: Seiches and lake currents
concepts.description: Explain seiches, wind-driven circulation, and Langmuir circulation and identify their effects on lake mixing and shorelines.

concepts.title: Wetland hydroperiod
concepts.description: Define hydroperiod and explain how water depth, duration, frequency, and seasonal inundation control wetland presence and vegetation.

concepts.title: Wetland classification
concepts.description: Distinguish marsh, swamp, bog, fen, and wet meadow by vegetation, hydrology, and minerotrophic versus ombrotrophic water source.

concepts.title: Hydric soils and redoximorphic features
concepts.description: Identify hydric soils and redoximorphic features such as gleying and mottling and explain their formation under anaerobic conditions.

concepts.title: Wetland ecosystem functions
concepts.description: Describe wetland ecosystem services, including flood attenuation, water-quality improvement, habitat provision, and carbon storage.

concepts.title: Paleochannel recognition
concepts.description: Recognize abandoned channels on floodplains from meander scars, oxbow fills, and subsurface sediment bodies.

concepts.title: Fluvial terraces as paleohydrologic record
concepts.description: Use terrace levels, sediment character, and stratigraphic position to infer past base-level change, climate shifts, and tectonic events.

concepts.title: Lake varves
concepts.description: Interpret varves as annual laminations in lake sediments and use varve counts to date lake sequences and past environmental changes.

concepts.title: Playa and paleolake deposits
concepts.description: Identify playa muds, evaporites, and paleoshorelines as evidence of former lake levels and changing aridity.

concepts.title: Speleothems as paleoclimate archives
concepts.description: Use speleothem growth layers and stable-isotope records to reconstruct past precipitation, temperature, and vegetation conditions.

concepts.title: Paleoflood slackwater deposits
concepts.description: Identify slackwater deposits and use them as paleostage indicators to estimate past flood stage and recurrence intervals.

concepts.title: Alluvial cut-and-fill sequences
concepts.description: Interpret cut-and-fill alluvial stratigraphy as evidence of alternating erosion and deposition driven by climate or tectonics.

concepts.title: Lake core paleoenvironmental proxies
concepts.description: Identify pollen, diatoms, charcoal, and grain-size changes in lake sediment cores as proxies for past vegetation, fire, and runoff.

concepts.title: Dating methods for freshwater sediments
concepts.description: Choose radiocarbon, optically stimulated luminescence, and tephrochronology to date freshwater deposits and interpret resulting age constraints.

topics.title: Human impacts, water quality, and freshwater monitoring

concepts.title: Dam and reservoir effects
concepts.description: Predict downstream changes in flow, sediment, temperature, and channel form caused by dams and reservoirs.

concepts.title: Urbanization and hydrograph change
concepts.description: Explain how impervious surfaces reduce infiltration and lag time and increase peak discharge, producing flashier urban hydrographs.

concepts.title: Agricultural impacts on water
concepts.description: Relate irrigation, tile drainage, fertilizer application, and livestock to water quantity changes and nutrient or sediment pollution.

concepts.title: Field water-quality parameters
concepts.description: Interpret temperature, pH, dissolved oxygen, turbidity, conductivity, and salinity measurements in freshwater monitoring.

concepts.title: Biochemical oxygen demand and oxygen sag
concepts.description: Apply biochemical oxygen demand and the oxygen sag curve to assess organic pollution and predict stream recovery downstream of a discharge.

concepts.title: Eutrophication and nutrient loading
concepts.description: Diagnose eutrophication from nitrogen and phosphorus loading, algal blooms, and hypoxic conditions and identify the limiting nutrient.

concepts.title: Point and nonpoint source pollution
concepts.description: Distinguish point-source from nonpoint-source pollution and identify common freshwater contaminants and their source pathways.

concepts.title: Water-table map construction
concepts.description: Construct water-table contour maps from well water-level measurements and determine gradient direction for monitoring or contamination assessment.

concepts.title: Stream monitoring station records
concepts.description: Interpret real-time and historical stage, discharge, and precipitation records from stream gaging stations to assess flow conditions and trends.

concepts.title: Macroinvertebrate bioassessment
concepts.description: Use benthic macroinvertebrate tolerance values and diversity indices to assess stream health and detect water-quality impairment.

concepts.title: Stormwater management and low-impact development
concepts.description: Describe low-impact development practices such as rain gardens, permeable pavement, and detention basins and their hydrologic goals.

concepts.title: Groundwater contaminant plumes
concepts.description: Identify contaminant plume behavior, distinguish point-source groundwater contamination, and interpret monitoring well data for plume tracking.
